newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian CCB approves link with CLF.
newsitem.headline: Belgian CCB approves link with CLF.

text.p: The towns and municipalities that own Belgium's Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) overwhelmingly approved on Monday plans for the bank to link with Credit Local de France and list part of its capital.
Credit Communal is Belgium's second largest bank, which also controls Luxembourg's Banque Internationale a Luxembourg.
The alliance with Credit Local de France will create Europe's 22nd largest banking group, baptised Dexia.
Under the banks' plan, each parent will set up a holding company in order to take a 50 percent stake in the partner's operational banks, which will keep their present names.
CCB Holding will remain in the grip of the bank's municipal shareholders, but between 25 and 30 percent ot its capital will be listed in an initial public offering on the Brussels bourse in November.
CLF Holding will continue to be owned by the French government and CLF's existing public shareholders, who approved the planned alliance last week.
